title: Acquisition Methods & Techniques 🔓
description: Master logical, filesystem, and physical acquisition – and how to handle locked devices.

slides.title: The Acquisition Pyramid 🔺
slides.content:
# Choosing the Right Method

Your choice depends on:
- Device model, OS version, and security patch level
- Whether the device is locked or unlocked
- Legal authority and consent
- Available tools and budget

From least to most intrusive:

**Logical → Filesystem → Physical**

The deeper you go, the more data you can recover, but the higher the risk of damaging the device or evidence.

quizData.question: Which acquisition method gives the most complete copy, including deleted data?
quizData.explanation: Physical acquisition creates a bit‑for‑bit image of the entire flash memory, including unallocated space.

slides.title: Logical Acquisition – Quick & Safe 💨
slides.content:
## Via Backup APIs

Most tools interact with the OS's backup mechanism:
- **Android**: `adb backup` (deprecated in recent versions), or custom apps that use content providers.
- **iOS**: iTunes‑style backup (unencrypted or encrypted).

**What you get:**
- Call logs, contacts, SMS/MMS
- App data (if app allows backup) – WhatsApp, SMS, etc.
- Media files (photos, videos)
- Some device settings

**Limitations:** No deleted data, no system logs, incomplete for many third‑party apps. Requires device to be unlocked and USB debugging enabled (Android) or trusted computer (iOS).

slides.title: Android ADB Backup Example
slides.content: If USB debugging is enabled and device is unlocked, create a backup:
slides.codeSnippet:
adb backup -apk -shared -all -system -f android_backup.ab
# -apk : backup APK files
# -shared : shared storage (SD card)
# -all : all apps (including non-system)
# -system : system apps

quizData.question: The `adb backup` command requires the device to have ___ enabled.
quizData.explanation: USB Debugging (Developer Options) must be enabled for ADB commands to interact with the device.

slides.title: Filesystem Acquisition – Going Deeper 📂
slides.content:
This method gains access to the device's root filesystem, often by:
- **Exploiting a temporary root** via bootloader unlock or a known vulnerability.
- **Using Checkm8 exploit** (iOS, up to iPhone X) for full filesystem access.
- **Flashing a custom recovery** (TWRP) on Android.

Once access is gained, you can copy partitions (e.g., `/data`, `/system`) or even create a dd image of the userdata partition.

**You get:** Deleted files (some), system logs, SQLite databases with journal files (can contain deleted records), app cache.

**Risks:** Can trigger anti‑tamper mechanisms, void warranty, and is legally sensitive. Always document the process.

quizData.question: Filesystem acquisition on Android always requires a physical chip‑off method.
quizData.explanation: It can be done via software exploits (temporary root) or an unlocked bootloader, without touching the chip.

slides.title: Physical Acquisition (Chip‑Off / JTAG / ISP) 🧬
slides.content:
## The Ultimate Extraction

When the device is locked, damaged, or encrypted, and no logical/filesystem access is possible, physical methods are used:
- **JTAG (Joint Test Action Group)**: Connects to test pins on the PCB to read memory.
- **ISP (In‑System Programming)**: Similar, using flash memory communication pins.
- **Chip‑Off**: Remove the NAND/eMMC chip and read it with a dedicated reader.

**Outcome:** A raw dump of the entire storage chip – unallocated space, deleted files, and sometimes decryption keys if the chip supports it.

**Challenges:** Extremely technical, permanent damage risk, must match the chip pinout, and encryption renders the dump useless without the key.

slides.title: ⚠️ Physical = Last Resort
slides.content: Chip‑off destroys the device. It should only be performed when absolutely necessary and by a qualified expert. Always obtain legal authorization.

quizData.question: Which physical acquisition technique requires removing the flash memory chip from the device?
quizData.explanation: Chip‑off involves physically desoldering the memory chip and reading it with an external programmer.

slides.title: Locked Devices & Bypass 🔐
slides.content:
If the device is locked:
- **Brute‑force** (slow, may trigger wipe).
- **Vulnerability exploitation** (e.g., GreyKey for iOS, Cellebrite UFED Advanced Services).
- **Legal methods**: compel suspect to unlock (biometrics or passcode, depending on jurisdiction).
- **Extraction via DFU/recovery mode** limited to filesystem if not encrypted.

Always consult legal counsel before attempting any bypass.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Capture the Screen

If the device is unlocked when seized, immediately photograph the screen. Disable auto‑lock and keep the device awake while you prepare acquisition. A screen capture can preserve open app states.
